issues.legal_issue: A writ of prohibition should not prevent a competent civil court from deciding the maintainability of a suit and its own jurisdiction when no exceptional ground for prohibition is established.
material_facts: The civil suit sought a declaration of title and possession, while the defendants contended that it was barred by statute and by res judicata or estoppel.
The civil court had power to decide its own jurisdiction and the maintainability of the suit, including as preliminary issues.

The High Court prohibited the civil court from proceeding without identifying a ground such as lack or excess of jurisdiction, breach of natural justice, an unconstitutional law, or violation of fundamental rights.
issues.conclusion: The writ prohibiting the civil court from proceeding was set aside, and the civil court was directed to decide the statutory-bar and res judicata or estoppel issues as preliminary issues.
issues.legal_principle: A writ of prohibition is ordinarily available where an inferior court or tribunal acts without or in excess of jurisdiction, in breach of natural justice, under an unconstitutional law, or in violation of fundamental rights. Its use is exceptional, must adhere to the governing principles of writ jurisdiction, and must not become an appeal in disguise or usurp the jurisdiction of a competent court to decide its own jurisdiction. The Court relied on U. P. Sales Tax Service Association v. Taxation Bar Association; Union of India v. Upendra Singh; T. C. Basappa v. T. Nagappa; Hari Vishnu Kamath v. Syed Ahmed Ishaque; Veerappa Pillai v. Raman & Raman Ltd.; and the principles discussed in Mirajkar v. State of Maharashtra and Ujjam Bai v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

rule.if: writ_seeks_to_stop_civil_suit and civil_court_can_decide_its_own_jurisdiction and not (patent_lack_or_excess_of_jurisdiction or natural_justice_breach or unconstitutional_law or fundamental_rights_violation)

predicates.writ_seeks_to_stop_civil_suit: A party seeks a writ preventing a civil court from proceeding with a suit.
predicates.civil_court_can_decide_its_own_jurisdict: The civil court has authority to consider the suit's maintainability and its own jurisdiction.
predicates.patent_lack_or_excess_of_jurisdiction: The civil court has proceeded, or is proceeding, in the face of a patent lack or excess of jurisdiction.
predicates.natural_justice_breach: The civil court has proceeded in breach of the rules of natural justice.
predicates.unconstitutional_law: The civil court has proceeded under a law that is unconstitutional.
predicates.fundamental_rights_violation: The civil court's proceeding contravenes a fundamental right.

issues.definition: When a writ seeks to stop a civil suit, the civil court can decide its own jurisdiction, and none of the listed exceptional defects is present, the civil court decides maintainability as a preliminary issue.

issues.legal_issue: A writ preventing a statutory appeal against a patta decision may remain in force while preliminary issues concerning the related civil suit are unresolved, with its continuation determined by the outcome of those issues.
material_facts: A statutory appeal challenged the grant of a patta to the respondents.
The related civil suit raised questions of maintainability and whether it was barred by res judicata or estoppel.
The Court considered the patta grant to be a formality following the earlier litigation and held that the appeal could be pursued only if the civil suit was maintainable and not barred.
issues.conclusion: The prohibition against proceeding with the statutory appeal was to remain in force until the preliminary issues in the civil suit were finally decided; it would be vacated if those issues were decided in favour of the appellants and confirmed if decided against them.
issues.legal_principle: Where the right to pursue a statutory appeal depends on whether a related civil suit is maintainable and barred by res judicata or estoppel, the appeal may remain stayed pending determination of those preliminary issues, with the prohibition's continuation dependent on their outcome.

predicates.statutory_appeal_challenges_patta_grant: A party has brought a statutory appeal challenging a patta grant.
predicates.related_civil_suit_preliminary_issues_ar: Preliminary issues about the maintainability of a related civil suit and whether it is barred remain undecided.

issues.definition: When a statutory appeal challenges a patta grant and preliminary issues in a related civil suit remain undecided, the statutory appeal remains stayed until those issues are resolved.

issues.legal_issue: A civil suit that in effect seeks to set aside or modify a decision made under the inam abolition legislation is barred unless the decision was obtained by misrepresentation, fraud, or collusion.
material_facts: Earlier proceedings under the inam abolition legislation had resulted in decisions concerning the land and a later patta grant.
The subsequent civil suit sought a declaration of title and possession, and the parties disputed whether it was in substance an attempt to set aside or modify the earlier decisions.
The Court left the application of the bar to the civil court, directing it to determine whether the suit was in effect brought to set aside or modify the earlier decisions.
issues.conclusion: The statutory bar and its application to the suit were to be considered by the civil court as a preliminary issue; the Supreme Court did not decide whether this suit fell within the bar.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1956 bars a suit or other proceeding in a civil court to set aside or modify a decision under that Act, except where the decision was obtained by misrepresentation, fraud, or collusion. The Court held that the Andhra Pradesh Act's provisions differ from those of the Tamil Nadu enactments and relied on the Andhra Pradesh line of authority, including Vatticherukuru Village Panchayat v. Nori V. Deekshithulu, Peddinti Venkata Murali Ranganatha Desika Iyengar v. Government of A.P., Pushpagiri Math v. Kopparaju Veerabhadra Rao, and S. Vanathan Muthuraja v. Ramalingam. It noted that Sri-La-Sri Sivaprakasa Pandara Sannadhi Avargal v. T. Parvathi Ammal had distinguished the Andhra Pradesh Act from the Tamil Nadu enactments.

rule.if: civil_suit_seeks_to_set_aside_or_modify_statutory_decision and decision_arose_under_inam_abolition_proceeding and not (misrepresentation_obtained_decision or fraud_obtained_decision or collusion_obtained_decision)

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_to_set_aside_or_modify_: A civil suit in substance seeks to set aside or modify a decision made in a statutory proceeding.
predicates.decision_arose_under_inam_abolition_proc: The decision the suit seeks to set aside or modify arose from a proceeding to determine rights under inam abolition legislation.
predicates.misrepresentation_obtained_decision: Misrepresentation was used to obtain the decision.
predicates.fraud_obtained_decision: Fraud was used to obtain the decision.
predicates.collusion_obtained_decision: Collusion between parties was used to obtain the decision.

issues.definition: If a civil suit in substance seeks to set aside or modify a decision from an inam abolition proceeding and none of the listed ways of obtaining the decision is present, the civil court lacks jurisdiction over the suit.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court should not quash an interim order that is not before it for consideration merely because it has set aside a writ prohibiting the underlying civil suit from proceeding.
material_facts: An interim injunction made by the civil court restrained the respondents from alienating the land and had been affirmed by an appellate court.
The appellants asked the Supreme Court to quash that injunction after arguing that the suit could not proceed.
The interim-order challenge was not before the Supreme Court, and the Court had not examined the orders.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to quash the interim orders, holding that it could not blindly quash orders of competent courts without considering them.
issues.legal_principle: A court should not set aside an order of a competent court without the order being before it and without examining it.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal_seeks_quashing_inte: A party asks the Supreme Court in an appeal to quash an interim order.
predicates.interim_order_not_before_supreme_court_f: The interim order is not before the Supreme Court for examination and review.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to quash an interim order in an appeal but the order is not before the Supreme Court for review, the Supreme Court does not quash it.
